PR #55 now adds a bounded local audition primitive plus normal /song controls for structurally verified managed WAV/MP3 material. Browser MIME is derived from inspected bytes rather than filename extension; external references, unsupported material and integrity failures do not receive fabricated playback.

Red-team review found the first media-admission rule was too weak: RIFF/WAVE magic alone and a bare ID3 header could masquerade as playable audio. The branch was repaired so WAV requires coherent RIFF chunk bounds plus valid fmt/data structure and MP3 requires a plausible MPEG audio frame, including after a bounded ID3v2 tag.

Audition authority is opaque and render-scoped. Consumer media URLs contain no raw Song/Version/Asset/profile ID, managed URI, hash or filesystem path. Every media read revalidates active Song, Version→Asset membership, Asset hash, managed-material integrity and supported audio structure before serving bytes.

HTTP delivery supports whole-file GET, HEAD and one bounded byte-range request for browser seeking; invalid ranges fail explicitly and unsatisfiable ranges return 416 with representation size. Delivery is streamed rather than loading the managed file into memory.

The shell CSP remains default-deny while adding media-src 'self'; Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy is same-origin. Opaque media grants expire on the next rendered page and fail closed if the active Song changes or managed bytes are tampered.

Audition remains read-only and explicitly does not implement loudness matching, instantaneous A/B, waveform/timeline, analysis, transcoding, Keep/Reject/Approve, generation, DAW/provider mutation, sharing/release or Gate-B listening acceptance.

Authored proof covers structural WAV/MP3 admission, fake RIFF/bare-ID3 rejection, range semantics, consumer controls, CSP/internal-path hiding, GET/HEAD/range delivery, grant expiry, stale-Song binding and tamper rejection.
